What's In the Works?

With so many changes to incorporate into the Finch and Softbill Save Pro-
gram the FSS Committee has not yet completed ali the new program en-
hancements. We will continue to work on enhancements to the program
and notify all members as these enhancements are incorporated into the
program. We are currently reviewing/working on:

The groupings of birds listed under the Group Managers section.
The incorporation of a breeding management software

The development of a yearly bloodline trade

The best format for Species Profiles

What YOU can do to make the program more successful:

All Finch and Softbill Save members are entitled to free classified advertising
in the NFSS Bulletin, on our society website (http://www.NFSS.org) and in
the FSS newsletter. We highly recommend that FSS members advertise
their available stock so that fellow FSS members can have access to any
available bloodlines. Presently, the program does not require FSS partici-
pants to sell their offspring to FSS members. We would like however to see
FSS members work together by using our free advertising and offering their
stock to fellow FSS members whenever feasible. Those who would like to
advertise but remain anonymous may contact the FSS Director for more
information.

We encourage ail FSS participants to recruit fellow hobbyists to join the
program. If anyone needs extra program materials to give to an interested
party, please do not hesitate to contact the FSS Director.

Contribute. Contribute. Contribute. If you have time on your hands and
experience with any of the birds included in the program apply for a Species
Captain or Group Manager position.

Tier Three and Beyond:

The Finch and Softbill Save Committee is currently working on incorporating
a Tier Three for the Finch and Softbill Save Program. Tier Three will be
geared towards those hobbyists who will adhere to strict record keeping,
the required use of specific breeding management software and the re-
quired trading of bloodlines on a yearly basis. This level of the program is
intended for individuals who may be looking to apply for a cooperative
breeding program permit from the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, or the
Canadian Wildlife Service and for those individuals who are very serious
about establishing a genetically viable captive bred population of bird spe-
cies. More information on Tier Three will be provided at a later date.

Breeder Recognition and Breeder of the Year Awards:

The 2002 Finch and Softbill Save program will incorporate recognition
awards for its participants. Group Managers and the Finch and Softbill Save
Committee will assist the FSS Director in choosing worthy participants to
award Breeder Recognition awards on a yearly basis. The NFSS Board of
Directors will choose a participant to award the Breeder of the Year award
with input provided by the F5S committee. To be eligible for such an award
you must be able to demonstrate breeding success with your registered
specie(s) and have completed ail FSS required quarterly reports. More de-
tails on eligibility will be forthcoming. Many have worked hard at establish-
ing species in aviculture and, will be honored for doing so.

Membership Fee:

In order to incorporate a newsletter, and breeder recognition and breeder
of the year awards we must have funds. Presently, the NFSS is not in a
position financially to fund these program changes. Awhile back a survey
was generated to test the waters and the vast majority of individuals had
no problem with paying a membership fee to participate in the Finch and
Softbill Save program provided the ideas presented were incorporated into
the program and that the membership fee paid was used solely for the pro-
gram. We have chosen through the help of tbe survey, to set the cost for
participation in the program at $15 yearly. All Finch and Softbill Save par-
ticipants must pay a $15 yearly membership fee and remain NFSS mem-
bers in good standing. Failure to renew your NFSS membership will result
in your expulsion from the Finch and Softbill Save Program, The member-
ship fee will be mailed in with your FSS application to the FSS Director,
made payable to NFSS.

Timor Zebra Finch Classification Committee

The Timor Zebra Finch Classification Committee including NFSS Panel Judges Julie Duimstra-
Chair, Paul Williams and Cecil Gunby. have been working on a proposal for proper entry of the
Timor Zebra within the NFSS Classifications. The committee's final proposal was received by this
office and submitted to the NFSS Board for review, consideration, and vote.

The Bird Safety Committee

in February, 2001, NFSS Judges Panel Director. Steve Hoppin, formed the Bird Safety Committee
to review and recommend procedure for show officials encountering a compromised finch or soft-
bill entered in the NFSS Division. The initial committee consisted of Sally Huntington-Chair, and
Dale Laird. Ms. Julie Ontmstra was invited to participate by committee chair. The committee
recommendation was received by this office and submitted to the NFSS oard for review, considera-
tion, and vote.
